experiment: VACASK's output into a pipe and into a pseudo-terminal (the VACASK runner, phase 2): an aborted analysis between two ops, its output into a file; a tran of about 4 s (long.sim) ended by SIGTERM and by SIGKILL 2 s in; the same tran through a pipe, an unsized pty and an 80-column pty (TestStdoutBuffering)
result: through a pipe (or into a file) VACASK's stdout is block-buffered: every line of a 4-7 s run arrives at exit, and a SIGTERM or SIGKILL loses the lines not yet flushed (none of the run's lines is left); through a pty each line arrives as printed; its progress bar needs a terminal width (simulator/progressbar.cpp: isTty, ttyColumns, 0 columns turning it off), so an unsized pty shows none and an 80-column one shows `|===== 91% ==== | <t>s @ <time>s`; everything, failures included, goes to stdout, stderr staying empty; per analysis it prints `Running analysis '<name>'.`, then `Elapsed time: <t>`, then that analysis's failure messages; the rows still in its file buffer when SIGKILL or SIGTERM ends it are lost, and rawfile.fix_points repairs the count from the rows on disk (as E40 assumed)
rules: §7.1: run_vacask reads VACASK through a pseudo-terminal where one opens (line-buffered, so the analyses are reported as they run; a pipe would hold every line until VACASK exits), sized 0 so no progress bar mixes into the narration
§7.1: an analysis's engine messages are the lines from its `Running analysis` line to the next one, after its elapsed line
§2.7 status 3: an interrupted VACASK run is converted after rawfile.fix_points (E40)
